subproblem.title: Simon Ch. 4, 2.2: the first variation of v(M, θ) is additive on C¹_c(U; ℝ^P)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n), and assume that x ↦ p_{T_xM}, the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x, is a.e. strongly measurable for H^n restricted to M. If X, Y : ℝ^P → ℝ^P are of class C¹ with compact supports and tsupport X, tsupport Y ⊆ U, then δV(X + Y) = δV(X) + δV(Y), where δV(Z) = R.firstVariation Z = ∫_M θ div_M Z dH^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (X Y : Euclid P → Euclid P), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) → ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 Y → HasCompactSupport Y → tsupport Y ⊆ U → R.firstVariation (X + Y) = R.firstVariation X + R.firstVariation Y
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof ("as DX = DX^T + DY and the trace is linear, R.firstVariation X = R.firstVariation X^T + ∫_M θ div_M Y dH^n", with the integrability justification given there); Simon Ch. 4, 2.2–2.3 (chapter-04.txt lines 132–147: δV(X) = ∫_M div_M X dμ_V, div_M X = Σ_j e_j·∇^M X^j), which is linear in X. Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, μ := H^n restricted to M (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), p(x) := orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x, div_M Z(x) := tangentialDivergence n M Z x = trace(p(x)∘DZ(x)), so that R.firstVariation Z = ∫ θ(x) div_M Z(x) dμ(x).
1. The trace functional. Let tr : L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) → ℝ, tr(A) := trace(A). It is linear on a finite-dimensional space, hence continuous (LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional), and div_M Z(x) = tr(p(x)∘DZ(x)) by definition. Moreover |tr(A)| ≤ P·‖A‖: expanding in the standard orthonormal basis (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner), tr(A) = Σ_j ⟨e_j, Ae_j⟩, and |⟨e_j, Ae_j⟩| ≤ ‖e_j‖·‖Ae_j‖ ≤ ‖A‖ because ‖e_j‖ = 1.
2. Integrability claim: if Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is C¹ with compact support and tsupport Z ⊆ U, then f_Z(x) := θ(x)·div_M Z(x) is μ-integrable.
 (a) Measurability. DZ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable); together with the hypothesis that p is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, x ↦ (p(x), DZ(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk). The map (q, A) ↦ tr(q∘A) is continuous (composition of operators is continuous, Continuous.clm_comp, followed by the continuous tr). Hence div_M Z is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable). The function x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable (R.measurable_mult composed with the cast ℕ → ℝ), so f_Z is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
 (b) Pointwise bound. DZ is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), so there is C with ‖DZ(x)‖ ≤ C for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). If x ∈ K := tsupport Z, then |div_M Z(x)| ≤ P·‖p(x)∘DZ(x)‖ ≤ P·‖p(x)‖·‖DZ(x)‖ ≤ P·C, because ‖p(x)‖ ≤ 1 for an orthogonal projection (Submodule.starProjection_norm_le) and by ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_comp_le. If x ∉ K, then DZ(x) = 0 (support_fderiv_subset: the support of DZ is contained in tsupport Z), so div_M Z(x) = tr(0) = 0. Since θ ≥ 0, |f_Z(x)| ≤ P·C·θ(x)·1_K(x) for every x.
 (c) Dominating function. K is compact (HasCompactSupport Z), closed and contained in U, so by R.locallyIntegrable_mult the lower integral of θ over M ∩ K with respect to H^n is finite. Since K is measurable, the lower integral of |θ·1_K| with respect to μ equals the lower integral of θ over K ∩ M with respect to H^n (Measure.restrict_restrict, then K ∩ M = M ∩ K), so θ is integrable for μ restricted to K (θ is measurable and nonnegative with finite lower integral there: integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top), hence θ·1_K is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff), and so is P·C·θ·1_K (Integrable.const_mul). By (a), (b) and Integrable.mono', f_Z is μ-integrable.
3. Pointwise additivity. X and Y are C¹, hence differentiable at every x, so D(X + Y)(x) = DX(x) + DY(x) (fderiv_add). Composition with p(x) and the trace are linear, so div_M(X + Y)(x) = div_M X(x) + div_M Y(x), and therefore θ(x)·div_M(X + Y)(x) = θ(x)·div_M X(x) + θ(x)·div_M Y(x) for every x.
4. Conclusion. By step 3 and additivity of the Bochner integral for integrable functions (integral_add, applicable by step 2 for Z = X and for Z = Y), R.firstVariation (X + Y) = ∫ (θ div_M X + θ div_M Y) dμ = ∫ θ div_M X dμ + ∫ θ div_M Y dμ = R.firstVariation X + R.firstVariation Y.
proof_key_steps: div_M Z(x) = trace(p(x)∘DZ(x)) with |trace A| ≤ P‖A‖ and ‖p(x)‖ ≤ 1.

For Z ∈ C¹_c with tsupport Z ⊆ U: θ·div_M Z is a.e. strongly measurable (measurable p, continuous DZ) and bounded by P·C·θ·1_{tsupport Z}, which is integrable by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; so it is integrable.
div_M(X + Y) = div_M X + div_M Y pointwise by linearity of the derivative, composition and trace.
Integrate and use integral_add: R.firstVariation (X + Y) = R.firstVariation X + R.firstVariation Y.

audit.reason: Projection measurability is an explicit hypothesis, so no undeclared sibling dependency is needed. The proof establishes measurable integrands, compactly supported derivative bounds and integrable domination using R.locallyIntegrable_mult. Pointwise derivative and trace additivity then legitimately permit integral_add. This proves precisely the stated identity without assuming integrability or linearity implicitly.

subproblem.title: Simon Ch. 4, 3.14: the explicit mean curvature field is measurable and bounded on compact subsets of U
subproblem.statement: Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P, U and O open subsets of ℝ^P, N ⊆ O with (closure(N) ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, pr : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) of class C¹ on O, and p : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) μ-a.e. strongly measurable with ‖p(x)‖ ≤ 1 (operator norm) for all x. Then there is H : ℝ^P → ℝ^P that is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, bounded on every compact K ⊆ U (there is Λ with ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Λ for all x ∈ K), and satisfies H(x) = Σ_{j=1}^P (Dpr(x)[p(x)e_j])^*(p(x)e_j) for every x ∈ N ∩ U, where e_1, …, e_P is the standard basis of ℝ^P, Dpr(x) is the derivative of pr at x and T^* is the adjoint of T ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (U N O : Set (Euclid P)) (pr p : Euclid P → (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P)), IsOpen U → IsOpen O → N ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 pr O → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → AEStronglyMeasurable p μ → (∀ x, ‖p x‖ ≤ 1) → ∃ H : Euclid P → Euclid P, AEStronglyMeasurable H μ ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ Λ : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ‖H x‖ ≤ Λ) ∧ ∀ x ∈ N ∩ U, H x = ∑ j : Fin P, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (fderiv ℝ pr x (p x (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))) (p x (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–5 of the parent proof (definition of H, measurability, local bound); Simon Ch. 4, 3.14 (chapter-04.txt lines 366–381) requires a μ_V-measurable H, and the bound on compact sets is the hypothesis 3.15 (chapter-04.txt line 385) used afterwards. Notation: E := ℝ^P, e_1, …, e_P the standard basis (EuclideanSpace.single j 1), T^* the adjoint of T ∈ L(E, E) (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint), Dpr(x) := fderiv ℝ pr x ∈ L(E, L(E, E)).
1. The algebraic map. Define F : L(E, L(E, E)) × L(E, E) → E by F(B, q) := Σ_j (B(qe_j))^*(qe_j). F is continuous: (B, q) ↦ qe_j and (B, q) ↦ B(qe_j) are continuous (evaluation of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous, Continuous.clm_apply), the adjoint is a linear isometric equivalence and hence continuous, evaluation (T, w) ↦ Tw is continuous, and a finite sum of continuous maps is continuous.
2. The set G := N ∩ U. We have N ∩ U = closure(N) ∩ U: the inclusion ⊆ is clear, and if z ∈ closure(N) ∩ U but z ∉ N, then z ∈ (closure(N) ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, which is impossible. Hence G is the intersection of a closed set and an open set, so it is Borel measurable.
3. Definition of H. Let H(x) := F(Dpr(x), p(x)) for x ∈ G and H(x) := 0 otherwise, i.e. H is the indicator of G applied to x ↦ F(Dpr(x), p(x)). For x ∈ N ∩ U this gives H(x) = Σ_j (Dpr(x)[p(x)e_j])^*(p(x)e_j), which is the third claimed property.
4. Measurability. The map x ↦ Dpr(x) is Borel measurable for every function pr (measurable_fderiv), and it takes values in a finite-dimensional normed space, so it is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Measurable.aestronglyMeasurable). With the hypothesis on p, x ↦ (Dpr(x), p(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk); composing with the continuous F (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable) and taking the indicator of the measurable set G (AEStronglyMeasurable.indicator) shows that H is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
5. Local bound. Let K ⊆ U be compact. The set K ∩ closure(N) is compact (IsCompact.inter_right) and, since K ⊆ U, it is contained in closure(N) ∩ U = N ∩ U (step 2), hence in N ⊆ O. Since O is open and pr is C¹ on O, Dpr is continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen), so there is C with ‖Dpr(x)‖ ≤ C for all x ∈ K ∩ closure(N) (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). Put Λ := P·max(C, 0) ≥ 0. Let x ∈ K. If x ∈ G, then x ∈ K ∩ closure(N), so ‖Dpr(x)‖ ≤ max(C, 0). For each j, u_j := p(x)e_j satisfies ‖u_j‖ ≤ ‖p(x)‖·‖e_j‖ ≤ 1, and ‖(Dpr(x)u_j)^*u_j‖ ≤ ‖(Dpr(x)u_j)^*‖·‖u_j‖ = ‖Dpr(x)u_j‖·‖u_j‖ ≤ ‖Dpr(x)‖·‖u_j‖² ≤ max(C, 0), since the adjoint preserves the operator norm (LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map). By the triangle inequality ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Σ_j max(C, 0) = Λ. If x ∉ G, then H(x) = 0 and ‖H(x)‖ = 0 ≤ Λ. Thus ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ K (this also covers K ∩ closure(N) = ∅ and P = 0), which is the second claimed property.
proof_key_steps: F(B, q) := Σ_j (B(qe_j))^*(qe_j) is continuous, and N ∩ U = closure(N) ∩ U is Borel.
H := 1_{N∩U}·F(Dpr(·), p(·)) has the required formula on N ∩ U and is a.e. strongly measurable (measurable_fderiv, measurability of p, continuity of F).
On compact K ⊆ U, K ∩ closure(N) is a compact subset of O where Dpr is continuous, so ‖Dpr‖ ≤ C there and ‖H‖ ≤ P·max(C, 0) on K.

audit.reason: The arbitrary-measure statement and pointwise operator-norm bound match the Lean type. Relative closedness makes N ∩ U measurable. The continuous algebraic map and measurable_fderiv establish the indicator field's a.e. strong measurability. Compactness of K ∩ closure N inside O bounds the derivative and yields P·max(C,0), including empty intersections and P = 0.

subproblem.title: Simon Ch. 2, 5.9 / Ch. 4, 2.7: the tangential divergence of the normal part of X is −X·H
subproblem.statement: Let P be a natural number, Q ≤ S linear subspaces of ℝ^P with orthogonal projections p_Q and P_S (Submodule.starProjection), pr : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), X, Y : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and x ∈ ℝ^P. Assume pr(x) = P_S, pr and X are differentiable at x, and Y(y) = X(y) − pr(y)(X(y)) for all y in a neighbourhood of x. Then trace(p_Q ∘ DY(x)) = −⟨X(x), Σ_{j=1}^P (Dpr(x)[p_Q e_j])^*(p_Q e_j)⟩, where e_1, …, e_P is the standard basis of ℝ^P (e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1), Dpr(x) ∈ L(ℝ^P, L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P)) is the derivative of pr at x, and T^* is the adjoint of T ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q S : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (pr : Euclid P → (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P)) (X Y : Euclid P → Euclid P) (x : Euclid P), Q ≤ S → pr x = S.starProjection → DifferentiableAt ℝ pr x → DifferentiableAt ℝ X x → Y =ᶠ[𝓝 x] (fun y => X y - pr y (X y)) → LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (Q.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ (fderiv ℝ Y x).toLinearMap) = -inner ℝ (X x) (∑ j : Fin P, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (fderiv ℝ pr x (Q.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))) (Q.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 2, 5.9 (chapter-02.txt lines 1326–1347: div_M X = div_M X^T − Σ_{i=1}^n X·B̄_y(τ_i, τ_i), B̄_y the second fundamental form of N at y) as used in Ch. 4, 2.7 (chapter-04.txt lines 185–209), at points where T_xM ⊆ T_xN. Notation: E := ℝ^P with the standard inner product; e_1, …, e_P the standard orthonormal basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun, e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1); p := p_Q = Q.starProjection and P_S = S.starProjection the orthogonal projections; for T ∈ L(E, E), T^* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T, characterised by ⟨T^*a, b⟩ = ⟨a, Tb⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left); A := DX(x) ∈ L(E, E); B := Dpr(x) ∈ L(E, L(E, E)); v := X(x).
1. Derivative of Y at x. Let Z(y) := X(y) − pr(y)(X(y)). Since Y = Z on a neighbourhood of x, DY(x) = DZ(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Since pr and X are differentiable at x, the map y ↦ pr(y)(X(y)) is differentiable at x (DifferentiableAt.clm_apply), and the product rule for evaluating an operator-valued map (HasFDerivAt.clm_apply; in fderiv form fderiv_clm_apply) shows that it has derivative h ↦ pr(x)(Ah) + (Bh)(v) at x, i.e. (pr x)∘A + B.flip v. With the difference rule (HasFDerivAt.sub) and pr(x) = P_S this gives DY(x)h = Ah − P_S(Ah) − (Bh)v for every h ∈ E.
2. Trace formula. For every C ∈ L(E, E), trace(p∘C) = Σ_j ⟨pe_j, C(pe_j)⟩. Proof: p(pw) = pw for all w, because pw ∈ Q and p fixes Q (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem, Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff); hence p∘C = p∘(p∘C). By cyclicity of the trace (LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'), trace(p∘(p∘C)) = trace((p∘C)∘p). Expanding the trace in the orthonormal basis (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner), trace((p∘C)∘p) = Σ_j ⟨e_j, p(C(pe_j))⟩, and self-adjointness of p (Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right) gives ⟨e_j, p(C(pe_j))⟩ = ⟨pe_j, C(pe_j)⟩.
3. One term. Fix j and put u := pe_j. Then u ∈ Q, hence u ∈ S because Q ≤ S, so P_S u = u. By step 1, ⟨u, DY(x)u⟩ = ⟨u, Au⟩ − ⟨u, P_S(Au)⟩ − ⟨u, (Bu)v⟩. Self-adjointness of P_S gives ⟨u, P_S(Au)⟩ = ⟨P_S u, Au⟩ = ⟨u, Au⟩, so the first two terms cancel. The adjoint identity for T := Bu and symmetry of the real inner product give ⟨u, (Bu)v⟩ = ⟨(Bu)^*u, v⟩ = ⟨v, (Bu)^*u⟩. Hence ⟨u, DY(x)u⟩ = −⟨v, (Bu)^*u⟩.
4. Summation. By steps 2 and 3 with C := DY(x), trace(p∘DY(x)) = Σ_j ⟨pe_j, DY(x)(pe_j)⟩ = Σ_j −⟨v, (B(pe_j))^*(pe_j)⟩ = −⟨X(x), Σ_j (Dpr(x)[pe_j])^*(pe_j)⟩, by linearity of the inner product in its second argument (inner_sum). This is the claim. For P = 0 all sums are empty and both sides are 0; the argument above covers this case.
proof_key_steps: DY(x) = DX(x) − P_S∘DX(x) − (h ↦ (Dpr(x)h)X(x)) by locality of the derivative and the product rule for y ↦ pr(y)(X(y)), using pr(x) = P_S.
trace(p∘C) = Σ_j ⟨pe_j, C(pe_j)⟩ from p² = p, cyclicity of the trace, the orthonormal-basis trace formula and self-adjointness of p.
For u = pe_j ∈ Q ≤ S: P_S u = u cancels ⟨u, DX(x)u⟩ − ⟨u, P_S DX(x)u⟩, and ⟨u, (Dpr(x)u)X(x)⟩ = ⟨X(x), (Dpr(x)u)^*u⟩ by the adjoint identity.
Summing over j gives trace(p∘DY(x)) = −⟨X(x), Σ_j (Dpr(x)[pe_j])^*(pe_j)⟩.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and the exact trace formula match. Local equality justifies differentiating Y; the evaluation product rule gives its derivative. Projection idempotence, trace cyclicity and Q ≤ S yield the stated cancellation, and the adjoint identity gives the correct sign. Summation completes the proof, including P = 0, without circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Simon Ch. 4, 2.7: a C¹_c(U) field equal to pr·X near N (the tangential part X^T)
subproblem.statement: Let U and O be open subsets of ℝ^P, N ⊆ O with (closure(N) ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, pr : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) of class C¹ on O, and X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U. Then there is X^T : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ with compact support and tsupport X^T ⊆ U such that, for every x ∈ N, X^T(y) = pr(y)(X(y)) for all y in some neighbourhood of x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U N O : Set (Euclid P)) (pr : Euclid P → (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P)) (X : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsOpen O → N ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 pr O → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ U → ∃ XT : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 XT ∧ HasCompactSupport XT ∧ tsupport XT ⊆ U ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, XT =ᶠ[𝓝 x] (fun y => pr y (X y))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof (the tangential part X^T := χ·pr·X; Simon Ch. 4, 2.7, chapter-04.txt lines 185–209, where X^T is C¹ with compact support in U and tangent to N at each point of N ∩ U), with cases (a) and (b) of step 8 merged into the single conclusion "X^T = pr·X near every point of N".
1. The compact set K. Put K := tsupport X ∩ closure(N). It is compact, being a closed subset of the compact set tsupport X (IsCompact.inter_right). K ⊆ N: if z ∈ K and z ∉ N, then z ∈ closure(N) ∖ N and z ∈ tsupport X ⊆ U, so z ∈ (closure(N) ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, which is impossible. Consequently K ⊆ W := O ∩ U (K ⊆ N ⊆ O and K ⊆ tsupport X ⊆ U), and W is open.
2. Cutoff function. ℝ^P is locally compact and regular. By exists_compact_closed_between there is a compact closed set L with K ⊆ interior(L) and L ⊆ W. By exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure applied to L ⊆ W there is an open set V with L ⊆ V, closure(V) ⊆ W and closure(V) compact. By exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (V open, L closed, L ⊆ V; smoothness order n = 1 in ℕ∞, which casts to ContDiff ℝ 1) there is χ : ℝ^P → ℝ of class C¹ with values in [0, 1], support χ = V, and z ∈ L ↔ χ(z) = 1 for every z. Hence tsupport χ = closure(V) is compact and contained in W, and χ = 1 on the open set interior(L) ⊆ L, which contains K.
3. Definition. Let X^T(y) := χ(y)·pr(y)(X(y)).
4. X^T is C¹. By contDiff_iff_contDiffAt it suffices to show that X^T is C¹ at every point y. If y ∈ O: O is open and pr is C¹ on O, so pr is C¹ at y (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt); X is C¹, so y' ↦ pr(y')(X(y')) is C¹ at y (ContDiffAt.clm_apply), and multiplying by the C¹ scalar function χ keeps it C¹ at y (ContDiffAt.smul). If y ∉ O: then y ∉ tsupport χ (since tsupport χ ⊆ W ⊆ O), so χ vanishes on a neighbourhood of y (notMem_tsupport_iff_eventuallyEq); hence X^T vanishes on a neighbourhood of y and is C¹ at y (contDiffAt_const.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
5. Support. If χ(y) = 0 then X^T(y) = 0, and χ(y) = 0 for every y ∉ closure(V) because support χ = V ⊆ closure(V). Hence X^T vanishes outside the compact closed set closure(V), so X^T has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro'), and tsupport X^T ⊆ tsupport χ = closure(V) ⊆ W ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left).
6. Agreement near N. Let x ∈ N. Case x ∈ tsupport X: then x ∈ K (as x ∈ N ⊆ closure(N)), so x lies in the open set interior(L), on which χ = 1; hence X^T(y) = 1·pr(y)(X(y)) = pr(y)(X(y)) for all y in the neighbourhood interior(L) of x. Case x ∉ tsupport X: X vanishes on a neighbourhood of x, and for y there X^T(y) = χ(y)·pr(y)(0) = 0 = pr(y)(0) = pr(y)(X(y)). In both cases X^T = (y ↦ pr(y)(X(y))) on a neighbourhood of x, which completes the proof.
proof_key_steps: K := tsupport X ∩ closure(N) is compact and, by (closure(N) ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, contained in N, hence in the open set O ∩ U.

Choose a C¹ cutoff χ with compact tsupport inside O ∩ U and χ = 1 on an open neighbourhood of K (exists_compact_closed_between, exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure, exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff).
X^T := χ·pr·X is C¹ near points of O (product rule) and vanishes near points outside tsupport χ, hence is C¹ with tsupport X^T ⊆ tsupport χ, compact and inside U.
At x ∈ N: χ = 1 near x if x ∈ tsupport X; otherwise X = 0 near x; in both cases X^T = pr·X near x.

audit.reason: The type includes every openness, regularity, relative-closure and support hypothesis. The compact set construction places the cutoff inside O ∩ U. The two local cases prove global C¹ regularity and agreement near every point of N, including points outside tsupport X. Compact support and containment in U follow as claimed.
